title: Layard finds the Library of Ashurbanipal at Nineveh

tellings.quote: in 1848 18 49 Austin Henry lard is Excavating the ancient city of Nineveh and what today is mosul Iraq

plain: In 1848 and 1849 the British archaeologist Austen Henry Layard dug up the ancient city of Nineveh, in what is now Mosul in Iraq, and found the library of Ashurbanipal, an Assyrian king whose collection of clay tablets held some of the oldest written stories. The researcher Matt LaCroix, who writes about lost ancient history, tells Michels this from his own reading, without naming a source, as the starting point for his argument about what those tablets remember of a time around 12,000 BC.
